lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62 (source read 2026-10-04); every envelope below is the source's, and each was also probed against a newer live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0) — differences are recorded in observed_divergences, never substituted

request.notes: Accepted types: `blocks` (to_task is not ready until from_task completes), `parent_child` (from_task is the parent; structural, never blocks), `discovered_from` (non-blocking) and `waits_on_gate` (to_task waits on the gate from_task). Every id goes through the SHARED resolver (`resolve_task_id`): a value of 36 or more characters is a full id and passes through untouched, a miss included, to this tool's own existence check; anything shorter than `MIN_PREFIX_LEN` (6) is `invalid_input`; anything between is searched as a PREFIX — matching nothing is the resolver's own `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …", a different message from this tool's own not-found, same code) and matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` (`AmbiguousIdPrefixError`, mapped by `tool_span`) with up to `AMBIGUITY_CANDIDATE_CAP` (5) `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS, the message stating the capped count. Every envelope is `{status, code, message}` plus, for that one code, `candidates` — the coordination errors here carry no other key. Every message names WHICH argument failed (`from_task_id` / `to_task_id`), and `from_task_id` is resolved first — a request with two bad ids is refused for the first one. Validation order (the tool body, then `upsert_task_edge`): BOTH ids are resolved first (from, then to), then the edge type, then the self-edge check on the RESOLVED ids, then existence, then the type-specific rules (`not_a_gate`, `parent_exists`, `cycle`). So `("x", "x", "blocks")` is the resolver's `invalid_input` for `from_task_id`, not `self_edge`, and an unknown type with a too-short id is `invalid_input` too — an earlier pass of this slice recorded the reverse order, wrongly. For `parent_child`, `parent_exists` is checked BEFORE the hierarchy cycle. A `cycle` is refused over the blocking edges (`blocks` + `waits_on_gate`, a dependency cycle) and over `parent_child` (a hierarchy cycle); the message names the new edge and then the cycle by FULL id, rendered from the new edge's SOURCE up its depends-on chain for a dependency cycle (`_find_edge_path(from, to, reverse=True)`, then `-> from`), and from its TARGET down the hierarchy for a hierarchy one (`_find_edge_path(to, from, reverse=False)`, then `-> to`). `discovered_from` is never cycle-checked. On an EXISTING (from, to, type) the call returns the same success payload as an insert, REPLACES that edge's metadata, and leaves `created_by` / `created_at` as they were — so those two fields are evidence of who inserted an edge (the receipt's "added by" on an already-existing relation). An edge write emits NO event, which is why Lens re-reads the focal task's edges before the call and evicts both endpoints' cached edges after it (T3-W8). Lens sends no `metadata` (REQUIREMENTS §5C.2); the canonical request above shows the field's shape, not Lens's policy, and `no_metadata` is the request Lens makes.

errors.message: edge type 'duplicates' is not accepted in this phase (accepted: ['blocks', 'discovered_from', 'parent_child', 'waits_on_gate']).
An edge cannot connect a task to itself.
from_task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
to_task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (from_task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.
a waits_on_gate edge requires the from_task (influx-ingest-cutover) to be a 'gate' task, got task_type='task'.
blocks edge influx-backfill -> influx-ingest-cutover would create a dependency cycle: influx-backfill -> influx-ingest-cutover -> influx-backfill
parent_child edge influx-backfill -> influx-epic would create a hierarchy cycle: influx-epic -> influx-backfill -> influx-epic
task influx-backfill already has a parent (influx-epic); a task may have at most one parent. Remove the existing parent_child edge before re-parenting.

observed_divergences: The success payload is `{success, from_task_id, from_title, to_task_id, to_title}`, the tool's return dict verbatim, and it is the same for an insert and for a metadata replacement (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT(from, to, type) DO UPDATE SET metadata = excluded.metadata`, which leaves `created_by` / `created_at` untouched) — so NOTHING in it says which happened: the residual T3 D11 states, and the upstream ask (a `created` flag) it would close. No event is emitted. The `task_not_found` for a full-length id names EVERY missing endpoint. **Live divergence:** the newer live server's `parent_exists` message names the removal tool — "… Remove the existing parent_child edge (lithos_task_edge_delete) before re-parenting." — a tool a4d2d62 does not have; the envelope above is the a4d2d62 text. The code and the named parent are what Lens reads, never the sentence. `invalid_edge_type` is treated as a Lens defect (the form offers only valid types). The `cycle` message is rendered verbatim; Lens never parses it for logic. The success payload itself is not probed live: it would write an edge into the operator's graph. Live check: the envelopes and order above were also probed (2026-10-04) against the Lithos this environment reaches, serverInfo 3.2.0 — NEWER than a4d2d62 (it serves `lithos_task_edge_delete`, added after 0.5.0) — with requests the server refuses, so nothing was written.
